title: Redwood <> Aegis GPU Systems - Partner Intro & Discovery
meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-23 / Start: 15:00 PST / Duration: 51m / Attendees: Maya Chen, Derek Alvarez, Priya Nair (Redwood); Ravi Malhotra, Sofia Martinez, Hiro Tanaka, Lena Park (Aegis GPU Systems)
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and Aegis GPU Systems to explore reseller and co-marketing partnership. Covered Aegis's global GPU hardware plans, preferred customer segments (finserv, genomics), compliance needs, integration surface (APIs, marketplace), and pilot ideas: benchmark joint workloads, dedicated pool offering, and a private deployment option. Action items include sharing security docs, a benchmark test plan, and scheduling an exec follow-up.
topics: Technical integration points: private deployment, VPC, on-prem, KMS
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'll kick us off. Um, looks like we have around 50 minutes, cool.
[00:00:12] Ravi Malhotra: Hey Maya, thanks for setting this up, we at Aegis are excited to explore how we might partner especially around dedicated GPU pools and system-level integration.
[00:00:25] Derek Alvarez: Great, Derek here on the SE side. We'll try to cover the high-level partner models and then dig into technical touchpoints. If at any point you want us to pause or demo, shout out.
[00:00:38] Sofia Martinez: Quick note, we have folks in EU and APAC — latency and region footprint is big for our customers.
[00:00:47] Maya Chen: Totally, that's one of the things we wanted to understand — your regional presence and where your customers need low latency vs where cost is primary.
[00:01:10] Lena Park: Our typical customers are enterprise finserv and genomics compute, both are sensitive — finserv wants <50ms for some inference endpoints, genomics is more throughput/batch oriented, cost sensitive.
[00:01:30] Derek Alvarez: OK, so two distinct workload patterns — Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments. For low-latency real-time endpoints we usually recommend dedicated pools in-region; for heavy throughput jobs batching and quantized models can lower cost.
[00:01:58] Hiro Tanaka: Can you explain what dedicated pools mean operationally? And how much isolation — eg for regulated workloads?
[00:02:10] Maya Chen: Sure, dedicated means reserved GPU capacity for a customer or partner offering. You get predictable throughput, isolation, and SLA targets. For regulated workloads we offer Private deployment which can sit in your VPC or on-prem with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs.
[00:02:34] Ravi Malhotra: That private option is interesting. Many of our sales discussions mention SSO/SAML, SOC 2, and sometimes on-prem for air-gapped.
[00:02:45] Derek Alvarez: We have SOC 2 and ISO artifacts; we'll share the security packet. For on-prem we provide an appliance-like package and the control plane can be customer-controlled. Key management via KMS or customer HSM is supported.
[00:03:02] Sofia Martinez: From integration perspective, how would this look — do you expose a standard REST API for inference or do partners integrate at a lower level into your runtime?
[00:03:15] Derek Alvarez: Primary integration is via the Redwood API — REST/SDKs for textgen, chat, embeddings. For deeper OEM integrations we also support deployment manifests and agents that can run in your infra and talk to the control plane.
[00:03:33] Maya Chen: For partner resale, we have a few models — referral, co-sell, and white-label dedicated stacks for some large partners. Curious what Go-to-Market you prefer.
[00:03:45] Lena Park: We like co-sell for large deals but want a clean resale/distribution path. Pricing needs to be clear and margin-friendly.
[00:03:56] Maya Chen: Totally — we can share a partner commercial matrix.
[00:04:10] [00:04:10] Derek Alvarez: On the technical side, could we run a short benchmark? Maybe a 2-hour run with finserv-style low-latency queries and a genomics batch job to show throughput. We'll provide a test plan.
[00:04:25] Ravi Malhotra: Yes, we'd want real numbers, and ideally if you could run both hosted and a dedicated pool comparison, plus quantized model runs.
[00:04:38] Derek Alvarez: We will. We typically test: cold-start latency, steady-state p99, tokens/sec for generation, and throughput for batch jobs. We'll include quantized and fp16 variants.
[00:04:50] Hiro Tanaka: Any caveats with model compatibility? Our customers often ask about model family support, LoRA, and custom weights.
[00:04:59] Derek Alvarez: Redwood supports a curated model catalog and can onboard custom models; LoRA/finetuned weights are supported in dedicated/private contexts. There may be kernel-specific optimizations for some architectures, and we'll surface supported variants.
[00:05:15] [00:05:15] Maya Chen: Also worth noting smart routing — requests can be routed by latency, cost, or region and fall back to compatible variants if capacity is constrained. That helps for multi-region partners.
[00:05:30] Sofia Martinez: On security docs — yes please send SOC 2, pen test summary, and the audit logging spec. For our enterprise buyers we also need data residency commitments.
[00:05:43] Maya Chen: We'll attach those. For residency you can pin private control planes in specific regions.
[00:06:05] Ravi Malhotra: How about billing models? Our finance team wants consolidated invoicing for resale.
[00:06:14] Priya Nair: We have partner billing options — resale with consolidated invoices or referrals via revenue share. We'll follow up with the partner commercial packet.
[00:06:24] [00:06:24] Derek Alvarez: Quick technical Q from our side — what GPUs do you primarily sell? Node types, memory, and NVLink, that kind of detail matters for perf expectations.
[00:06:36] Ravi Malhotra: Our fleet is mixed — we have A100 80GB equivalents, H100 clusters in some regions, and a custom Ampere box. We're also exploring DGX-like offerings.
[00:06:51] Derek Alvarez: Good to know — we'll tune the benchmark plan to those SKUs. H100s will show better perf on certain model families; A100 with 80GB is still solid for long context.
[00:07:05] Hiro Tanaka: Any recommended quantization profiles? Our customers want smaller footprints to lower cost.
[00:07:13] Derek Alvarez: We recommend 4-bit or 8-bit quantization depending on architecture and the model. We'll propose a set of quantization profiles and expected perf/quality tradeoffs. We also have Redwood Optimize that suggests config for batching and quantization.
[00:07:30] [00:07:30] Maya Chen: For pilot scope — propose: 1) Share security/commercial docs, 2) Run a 2-week benchmark including hosted vs dedicated vs quantized runs, 3) Joint GTM plan draft for co-sell. Does that sound reasonable?
[00:07:49] Lena Park: Yes, and add a joint case study template.
[00:07:55] Maya Chen: Will do.
[00:08:10] Ravi Malhotra: On legal — our procurement will want reseller terms and SLAs. We may need a papering window of 6-8 weeks.
[00:08:22] Maya Chen: Understood — we'll include a sample MSA and SLA in the packet.
  [00:08:40] Sofia Martinez: A small tech aside — how do you handle KV cache and prefix caching for conversational agents? We do a lot of retrieval-augmented workflows.
[00:08:53] Derek Alvarez: We have KV cache management and automatic prefix caching; for RAG we'd recommend embeddings endpoints combined with prefix caching for repeated context. Also continuous batching reduces per-token cost while keeping latency SLOs.
[00:09:12] Hiro Tanaka: Great. Any reference customers in finserv or life sciences?
[00:09:20] Maya Chen: We can share anonymized case studies and references; I'll add that to the docs.
[00:09:33] [00:09:33] Ravi Malhotra: Ok next steps then, timeline? We'd like to run benchmarks next month if possible.
[00:09:41] Maya Chen: We can start planning this week; SE will send test plan by Friday and propose dates for the run.
[00:09:50] Priya Nair: I'll coordinate GTM contacts.
[00:09:56] [00:09:56] Maya Chen: Anything else from Aegis?
[00:09:59] Lena Park: No, that's it.
[00:10:03] Maya Chen: Alright thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and plan.
[00:50:30] [closing] Maya Chen: Closing notes — thanks all, expect email with docs and benchmark plan.
